column1: # Performance budgets (implementation-plan.md rule P6). `cargo xtask bench` builds the
# benchmark examples in release mode and fails if any budget is exceeded.
# Columns: benchmark, measurement, rule, bound, rationale.
#   rule `max_ns`:   the measurement in ns/op must not exceed `bound`.
#   rule `ratio_to`: the measurement must not exceed `bound` x the named measurement
#   rule `ratio_host`: the row is also measured with the benchmark built against the host C
#                    library (dynamically linked, as `--compare` builds it; rebuilt only when the
#                    benchmark's source changes), in the same `cargo xtask bench`, over N rounds
#                    (`--runs`, default 5) after a warm-up round. `bound` is the TARGET (a ratio,
#                    1.10: within about 10% of glibc, owner 2026-10-05); a miss is printed and never
#                    fails the run. The regression GATE is separate: `bench/host_limits.tsv` holds,
#                    per CPU model (the `model name` line of /proc/cpuinfo, not the host name), a
#                    limit on the same-run MEDIAN Liella/glibc ratio of the row. A CPU with no entries
#                    is measured and reported, never gated. The worst ratio (slowest Liella round /
#                    fastest glibc round) is printed as a diagnostic only.
# Absolute bounds are deliberately loose (they catch order-of-magnitude regressions on any
# x86_64 machine); the ratios carry the design claims.
